== PHASE 5 TITLE/ABSTRACT SCREENING RULES (`PROTOCOL.md` §6 & `INCLUSION_EXCLUSION.md`) ==
Screen this record at the Title/Abstract stage against all eligibility criteria:
1. `c1_service_access`: Household or community water or sanitation service access? (Not pure agricultural irrigation, hydropower, ambient river ecology, flood control, or non-water topics.)
2. `c2_legal_admin_narrow`: Under the **2026-10-13 narrow rule-type reading**, does the study examine (or plausibly examine on full text) a legal, administrative, regulatory, tenure/documentation, tariff/cost-recovery/subsidy, discretion/accommodation, enforcement/disconnection, or utility-ownership/regulatory-structure mechanism governing service access? (Not generic project delivery, pure behavioural handwashing promotion, or unanalysed macro-governance background.)
3. `c2_legal_admin_plain`: Under the **literal/plain wording of Criterion 2**, does it examine ANY legal, administrative, institutional, regulatory, or governance factor?
4. `c3_empirical_or_systematic_review`: Empirical primary evidence (quantitative, qualitative, mixed-methods, socio-legal empirical) OR a systematic empirical synthesis/meta-analysis? (Not a pure commentary, editorial, or doctrinal essay with clearly no empirical data.)
5. `c4_access_outcome`: An outcome relevant to water/sanitation access, connection, coverage, availability, reliability, continuity, quantity, quality-as-service-access, affordability, or exclusion?

Decision rules at Title/Abstract stage:
- `"include"`: Clearly meets (or strongly appears to meet) all criteria from title + abstract.
- `"unsure"`: Plausibly in scope on water/sanitation service access + legal/administrative/institutional/regulatory mechanism, such that the full text MUST be retrieved to determine eligibility; do NOT prematurely exclude ambiguous socio-legal, informal-settlement, tariff, or utility-governance abstracts!
- `"exclude"` + ONE primary exclusion code (`E01` wrong topic, `E02` wrong population, `E03` wrong exposure, `E04` wrong outcome, `E05` no empirical evidence, `E06` engineering only, `E07` wrong service, `E08` duplicate, `E09` insufficient information, `E11` wrong jurisdiction/context, `E12` wrong study design): Title + abstract clearly fail at least one criterion.
- Record BOTH `decision` (under the active narrow rule-type Criterion 2 reading) AND `plain_criterion2_decision` (what your Phase 5 call would be under the literal broad Criterion 2 wording).
- Provide 1 to 3 exact verbatim substrings (`>= 20` characters, zero `...` ellipses, zero paraphrasing) from `== TITLE AND ABSTRACT ==` in `evidence_quotes`.

evidence_quotes.quote: Development of Information Focal Points (IFPs) on Community Water Supply in Rural Areas: An Initiative to Disseminate Research Results

At the end of 1998 a training workshop was organized by the IRC International Water and Sanitation Centre in The Hague, The Netherlands, with the aim of establishing Information Focal Points (IFPs) within a number of organizations.
This article describes the objectives and outcomes of the above workshop and provides thumbnail sketches of the partner organizations involved in the sub-project.

raw_response.plain_vs_narrow_note: Excluded under both narrow and plain readings: the article reports on a research-dissemination training workshop to set up organizational Information Focal Points rather than examining any legal, administrative, regulatory, or governance factor shaping water service access, and it also lacks empirical primary evidence or service-access outcomes.
raw_response.rationale: Although situated in the general field of rural community water supply, this article describes a 1998 training workshop organized to establish Information Focal Points (IFPs) within four partner NGOs/research centres to disseminate research results. It fails Criterion 2 (E03: research dissemination and documentation initiative rather than a legal or administrative mechanism governing water access), Criterion 3 (descriptive workshop report providing organizational thumbnail sketches and implementation plans rather than an empirical study or systematic review), and Criterion 4 (no household or community water access outcome).
